# Table

A sortable, scrollable table component that loads data on demand from a backing database table. JavaScript returns DOM; Python returns a serializable View.

<template v-if="language === 'js'">

## table {#table-method}

`table(options)`

Creates a [Table](#table-class), connects it to the active coordinator and returns its containing HTML element. An explicitly supplied vgplot API context determines its coordinator; the mosaic-inputs helper uses the global coordinator.

</template>

<template v-else-if="language === 'python'">

## table_input

`vg.table_input(source: Any, bind: Any = None, columns: Any = None, filter_by: Any = None, width: Any = None, height: Any = None, max_width: Any = None, row_batch: Any = None, align: Any = None, **opts: Any)`

Create a serializable table widget view from a source name or parameter.

Python input helpers return serializable View objects, rather than DOM widgets or MosaicClient instances. The bind argument serializes as as, source serializes as from, and other keyword names use camel case. Options whose value is None are omitted before aliases are applied; for example menu(bind=selection, as_=None) retains the bind argument. False, zero and empty strings remain present. Unknown keyword options are retained for custom clients.

</template>

## Declarative options

The declarative input discriminator and from source are required. The source can be a table name or a parameter reference. Native JavaScript permits an omitted options object; Python requires its source argument but accepts Any values beyond the declarative schema. A source Param reinitializes metadata and table data when its value changes.

| Option | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | Yes | A table grid widget. |
| `as` | No | The output selection. A selection clause is added for each currently selected table row. |
| `from` | Yes | The name of a database table to use as a data source for this widget. |
| `columns` | No | A list of column names to include in the table grid. If unspecified, all table columns are included. |
| `filterBy` | No | A selection to filter the database table indicated by the `from` property. |
| `align` | No | An object of per-column alignment values. Column names should be object keys, which map to alignment values. Valid alignment values are: `"left"`, `"right"`, `"center"`, and `"justify"`. By default, numbers are right-aligned and other values are left-aligned. |
| `width` | No | If a number, sets the total width of the table widget, in pixels. If an object, provides per-column pixel width values. Column names should be object keys, mapped to numeric width values. |
| `maxWidth` | No | The maximum width of the table widget, in pixels. |
| `height` | No | The height of the table widget, in pixels. |
| `rowBatch` | No | The number of rows load in a new batch upon table scroll. |

The output binding is a Selection. Python's table_input widget is distinct from the table data-definition helper. The input parser and JavaScript helper use the wire name table; Python code generation uses table_input.

## Table {#table-class}

`new Table(options)`

Native JavaScript class extending [MosaicClient](../core/client). Its `element` property contains the widget DOM. The constructor accepts the native helper options. Python does not export this runtime class.

Native defaults are wildcard columns `*`, height 500 pixels and rowBatch 100. Each instance receives a fresh default columns array. Columns and per-column alignment/width maps retain their supplied order and values.

Click a column header to sort ascending, click again to sort descending, and meta-click the current header to cancel sorting. Scrolling near the bottom requests the next batch. These are runtime interactions rather than declarative sort properties. Row selection uses pointer hover and clears on pointer leave.

Native JavaScript tables accept an existing container element; declarative definitions do not serialize DOM nodes.

Native JavaScript tables accept per-column formatting functions returning text or DOM nodes. Hovering nested formatter elements selects their containing table row. Declarative definitions do not serialize callbacks.

## Coordinator and paging lifecycle

Metadata, visible pages and look-ahead prefetch use the table's owning coordinator, including an explicitly scoped vgplot API context. Source and filter changes cancel obsolete requests and restart from the first page. Disconnection cancels pending table and prefetch requests.

## Executable starters

Shared starters cover default columns, ordered projection/alignment/width, scrolling batches, row selection, linked filtering and a source Param switching between two named datasets. Native formatting and explicit scoped coordinators have JavaScript-only starters; JSON/YAML do not invent callback or coordinator fields.
